title: Familial hypercholesterolemia Southern blot: son inherited the 8 kb mutant band
vignette: A 34-year-old man is found to have an LDL level of 310 mg/dL and a normal serum triglyceride level. His father suffered a myocardial infarction at age 39, and his paternal grandfather died of a heart attack at age 40. The patient's wife has a normal lipid profile. DNA samples are obtained from several family members for genetic analysis. Southern blotting of restriction fragments from a region containing the LDL receptor gene shows the following pattern: the patient's lane has a 12 kb and an 8 kb band; the wife's lane has only a 20 kb band; the son's lane has a 20 kb and an 8 kb band; the brother's lane has a 12 kb and a 10 kb band; and the father's lane has a 10 kb and an 8 kb band. Which of the following statements best describes the DNA analysis results?

clues.note: Markedly elevated LDL (310 vs normal <100 mg/dL) with normal triglycerides in a young adult suggests heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (LDL receptor defect).

clues.text: father suffered a myocardial infarction at age 39
clues.note: Premature coronary disease in a first-degree relative supports an inherited (autosomal dominant) hypercholesterolemia; the father is affected.

clues.text: paternal grandfather died of a heart attack at age 40
clues.note: Premature CAD across successive generations (grandfather -> father) fits AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT vertical transmission of familial hypercholesterolemia.

clues.text: the patient's lane has a 12 kb and an 8 kb band
clues.note: On the blot the affected patient and his affected father share the 8 kb band, which therefore marks the mutant LDL receptor allele; the son also carries the 8 kb band.

whatMatters: The patient and his affected father BOTH carry the 8 kb band, so the 8 kb restriction fragment marks the MUTANT LDL receptor allele (familial hypercholesterolemia, autosomal dominant). The patient's SON also has the 8 kb band, so he most likely INHERITED the mutation. Answer E.
strategy: Find the band shared by the two people known to be AFFECTED (patient + father) = 8 kb = mutant allele. Then see who else carries it: the son does -> he inherited the mutation. Reject 10 kb/12 kb as the mutant band (the patient, who is affected, must carry it - he lacks 10 kb; the 12 kb is shared with the unaffected-pattern brother), reject X-linked (father-to-son transmission would be impossible for X-linked, and FH is autosomal dominant), and reject 'brother inherited it' (brother lacks the 8 kb band).

options.text: The disease is transmitted in an X-linked recessive fashion
The mutation is probably located in the 10 kb band
The mutation is probably located in the 12 kb band
The patient's brother most likely inherited the mutation
The patient's son most likely inherited the mutation

eliminations.label: X-linked recessive - contradicted by inheritance/disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: transmission on the X chromosome from carrier mothers to sons. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: familial hypercholesterolemia is AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, and father-to-son transmission (grandfather->father->patient) cannot occur with X-linked inheritance. ✅ Correct if: a true X-linked pedigree (no male-to-male transmission).

eliminations.label: Mutation in 10 kb band - patient lacks it
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: assigning the mutation to the 10 kb fragment. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the affected PATIENT does not have a 10 kb band, so the mutant allele cannot be the 10 kb segment (the brother inherited the 10 kb band from the father and is not affected). ✅ Correct if: the affected individuals shared the 10 kb band.

eliminations.label: Mutation in 12 kb band - shared with unaffected pattern
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: assigning the mutation to the 12 kb fragment. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the 12 kb band is shared by the patient and his brother, but the father (affected) lacks 12 kb; the segment common to both affected people (patient + father) is the 8 kb band. ✅ Correct if: both affected individuals shared the 12 kb band.

eliminations.label: Brother inherited the mutation - he lacks 8 kb
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: claiming the brother carries the mutant allele. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the brother's lane shows 12 kb and 10 kb but NOT the 8 kb mutant band, so he did not inherit it. ✅ Correct if: the brother's lane contained the 8 kb band.

reasoning: Very high LDL + premature CAD across generations = autosomal dominant familial hypercholesterolemia
The two known-affected people (patient and father) share the 8 kb band -> 8 kb marks the mutant LDL receptor allele
The patient's son also carries the 8 kb band
-> the son most likely inherited the mutation; answer E
mechanism: Heterozygous FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA is an AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT LDL-receptor defect causing markedly elevated LDL and PREMATURE atherosclerosis (myocardial infarction at young ages across generations). SOUTHERN BLOTTING detects DNA sequence differences: genomic DNA is cut by restriction enzymes, fragments are separated by gel electrophoresis (larger fragments migrate slower), transferred to a membrane, and hybridized with a labeled DNA PROBE complementary to the LDL receptor gene, revealing band patterns. Because a mutation can create or destroy a restriction site, the mutant allele produces a distinctively sized fragment. Here, the two individuals known to be AFFECTED - the patient and his father - both carry the 8 kb band, identifying the 8 kb restriction fragment as the MUTANT LDL receptor allele. The patient's SON also carries the 8 kb band, so he most likely inherited the mutation and is at risk. The brother inherited the father's 10 kb (non-mutant) band and lacks the 8 kb fragment; father-to-son transmission also excludes X-linked inheritance.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biochem/Genetics > Southern blot (DNA): restriction digest -> electrophoresis -> probe hybridization; familial hypercholesterolemia = autosomal dominant LDL receptor defect, premature CAD; mutant allele = band shared by affected individuals.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Band shared by affected patient + affected father (8 kb) = mutant allele; son has it -> inherited it.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Southern blot, restriction fragment, probe hybridization, familial hypercholesterolemia, or autosomal dominant? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: 10 kb/12 kb aren't shared by BOTH affected people; brother lacks 8 kb; father-to-son transmission excludes X-linked.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Southern blot (stem image): compare lanes - the 8 kb band is common to the two affected members (patient + father), marking the mutant allele; the son carries it -> inherited the mutation.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: on a linkage blot, the mutant allele = the band shared by affected individuals; trace it to at-risk relatives.

keywords.back: Band shared by the AFFECTED individuals

Genetics > autosomal dominant LDL receptor defect; premature CAD.

memoryHook: On a family blot, the band that shows up in everyone who's sick IS the disease - here the 8 kb band; the son carries it, so he's inherited the bad LDL receptor.
